Welcome to Wordsworth Primary
and Nursery School Welcome to Wordsworth Primary and Nursery School Welcome to Wordsworth Primary School - a happy, caring place where every child is known, valued and encouraged to succeed. At Wordsworth, we believe that together we nurture individuals, inspire all minds and prepare every learner to thrive. Our strong values are at the heart of daily life in our school. Curiosity inspires a love of learning, determination gives us the confidence to keep going. kindness helps us care for one another and communication helps us build positive relationships. By being Ready, Respectful and Safe, we create a calm, supportive environment where children feel secure, confident and ready to learn. We pride ourselves on working closely with families and celebrating every child's achievement. We are proud of our inclusive ethos and our commitment to nurturing the whole child - academically, socially and emotionally. At Wordsworth Primary School, every child is encouraged to believe in themselves, celebrate their individuality and develop the skills they need for the future. Thank you for taking the time t o learn about our school. W e look forward to welcoming you and working together t o ensure every child at Wordsworth flourishes. Mrs Annette Hixon Headteacher Attendance Safeguarding SEND Behaviour Nursery Our Vision At Wordsworth we believe that together we nurture individuals, inspire all minds and prepare every learner to thrive. Our strong values are at the heart of daily life in our school. Curiosity inspires a love of learning, determination gives us confidence to keep going, kindness helps us to care for one another, and communication helps us to build positive relationships. Partnerships Hamwic Education Trust Wordsworth Primary and Nursery Schooll is part of Hamwic Education Trust - one of the largest multi-academy trusts in the South of England. Its academies work in local community partnerships based in Southampton, Portsmouth, Poole and East Dorset. Hamwic Education Trust celebrates the uniqueness of pupils, staff and schools, and aims for everyone to achieve their full potential through the pathways of opportunities available. Music Lessons
Information for Parents
Music Lessons
Music lessons, academic year 2026-27 – Wordsworth
SIOW Music are providing instrumental lessons at Wordsworth Primary from September 2026.
Lessons are available on the following instruments (subject to availability) for Y3-Y6 pupils.
Brass (trumpet, cornet)
Woodwind (flute, clarinet)
Violin (also available to Y2 pupils)
The cost of lessons are as follows (all lessons are 20 minutes and take place during the school day);
Group - £75 per term (or £210 if paid in full by 31st August 2026)
Paired - £125 per term (or £345 if paid in full by 31st August 2026)
Individual - £190 per term (or £495 if paid in full by 31st August 2026)
All Pupil Premium students will only need to pay £30 and the rest of the cost will be covered by the school (group lessons only)
Pupils with a EHCP can access an individual lessons at the paired lesson cost. All Looked After Children will receive an individual lesson fully funded by SIOW Music.
We are able to provide instruments for £50 per year.
If you would like details on how to sign up for lessons then please email graham.hesp@southampton.gov.uk

pageCache.text:
After School Clubs
Information for Parents
After School Clubs
At Wordsworth we offer a range of after school clubs for children to enjoy which are either run by the School or by an external provider. Some of these clubs may be at lunchtime and some will be after school. A limited number of free clubs run by teacher volunteers will change regularly and some of them may be offered initially to 'invited' children, for example pupil premium children. Outside agency clubs usually remain the same all year and do carry a cost. Please click on the relevant links below for more information.
TEAM SPIRIT - After school club sports coaching
Here are the clubs we run:
Monday Football Yr 1/2/3 (boys and girls mixed)
Tuesday Team Xtreme Yrs 1-6
Thursday Basketball Yrs 1-6
Friday Football Yrs 4/5/6 (boys and girls mixed)
All Team Spirit club bookings can be made by contacting us directly on 02380 658636. The same coach will be working with the children on a week to week basis ensuring continuity which is essential in a child's development.
Please contact sports director Ryan Hinton for further information on Team Spirit courses by clicking the link below.
https://teamspirit4sport.co.uk/courses
Lego Club supplied by Kids With Bricks
We are pleased to be able to offer our Kids With Bricks after school club running from 3.30pm - 4.30pm every Monday. This club is open for Years 1 & 2 and there are a maximum of 12 places available. We also run a KS2 group 3.30pm - 4.30pm every Wednesday for 5 weeks. This club is open for Years 3, 4, 5 & 6 and there are a maximum of 12 places available also.
The club is organised, administered and supported by Kids With Bricks Ltd, an external provider who deliver after school clubs across the whole of the UK. As well as completing a range of exciting educational challenges, students will have the chance to work both individually and to work in teams. BOOK ONLINE!
The club costs are available on the Kids with Bricks website and is paid for half termly in advance. All club places are reserved and paid for online. Just go to Kids With Bricks to book your child’s place. Any problems please contact us on 01633 383211 or bookings@kidswithbricks.com.
You will be notified by email when the next load of dates are available to book.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care | Wordsworth Primary and Nursery School
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
Information for Parents
Wraparound Care
DFE Funded Breakfast Club
We are delighted to share with you that are offering this free breakfast club to all our children within our primary school from Reception to Year 6, that is being funded by the Department for Education (DFE).
Wordsworth is be one of 2,000 schools that joined this scheme in September 2026, demonstrating our commitment to:
giving every pupil, regardless of their background the best start in life
breaking down the barriers to every child achieving and thriving at school and in later life, by ensuring they are ready to learn, supporting parents to work and tackling poverty
The breakfast club run's from 8.15am to 8.45am each day, where children will be provided with a free breakfast and a soft start into the school day, so that they are ready for their school day to start at 8.50am. We ask that children arrive as close to 8:15 as possible, unfortunately, children will not be able to join the breakfast club if they arrive after 8.30am.
A buffet style breakfast will be providing in the hall in line with the school food standards for England.
The breakfast club is run by our Wordsworth staff team known to the children. If you have any questions, please contact the office.
Kidzplay provides Breakfast and After School Clubs throughout Hampshire and offer a breakfast club and afterschool club at Wordsworth Primary and Nursery School.
With 7 clubs, we offer Ofsted registered childcare for children aged 4 – 11 years.
We strive to promote a happy and relaxed atmosphere, where parents are confident to leave their children.
If you would like to know more about Kidzplay please get in touch, we look forward to hearing from you.

pageCache.pageTitle: Medical & First Aid  | Wordsworth Primary and Nursery School
pageCache.text:
Medical & First Aid
Information for Parents
Medical and First Aid
School Medical Service
The school doctor, nurse and dentist make regular visits to school. If your child has not had a pre-school medical he/she will see the school nurse in their second term. Regular checks are made on children's sight, hearing and teeth. You will be informed beforehand and invited to attend if necessary.
Medication
If your child requires medication prescribed by his/her doctor we can administer this at the required times throughout the school day, simply bring the medicine to the school office in the original box with the dispensing label intact and complete a Medical Administration form. Please note, we can only administer over the counter medication by completing the same form, indicating why your child needs to have this. The Medical Administration form can be obtained from the main office.
Inhalers
If your child has an inhaler in school, please ensure it is in its box, so we can identify who it belongs to with the dispensing label intact.
If your child uses an AeroChamber or Spacer, ensure you collect this at the end of every half-term, to be cleaned and checked and bring back at the start of the new term.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum Enrichment Opportunities
Curriculum Enrichment Opportunities
At Wordsworth Primary School and Nursery, we work hard to ensure that there are many curriculum enrichment opportunities to bring learning to life for our children, developing lifelong learners. During their time here, the children will experience a range of trips and visits within Shirley, Southampton and Hampshire, and they will travel as far as Dorset and London. In addition to this, we invite visitors to our school to bring the curriculum to life. For example, in Year 2 the children experience the Florence Nightingale Outreach Workshop and in Year 3 the children experience ‘Portals to the Past – The Stone Age’.
Residential Trips
Our children have the opportunity to participate in two residential school trips during their time at Wordsworth. In Year 4 the children visit Home Farm for a two-night stay and in Year 6 the children visit Avon Tyrrell Outdoor Activity Centre for a four-night stay.
Home Farm, Year 4 Residential photos below.
Science - Year 3
Year 3 had some volunteers from the University of Southampton come in for six weeks to teach them about healthy eating, sustainability, recycling and an alternative method of planting and growing called Hydroponics.
The children planted lettuce and cucumber seedlings using the hydroponic tank, water and nutrients.
Author Visit - Yarrow Townsend
During the Summer term Year 5 and 6 were fascinated by a visit from the new author Yarrow Townsend, who told us all about her life and how her experiences gave her inspiration for her stories. They felt really inspired to write their own adventure stories.
Side Note - She told us her mum came to Wordsworth when it was an infant school!
Sports Events
In addition to Sports Day, each year, children participate in the Hamwic JEP Schools Sports event held at Upper Shirley High with children from other Hamwic schools. They participate in several activities such as shuttle runs, hurdles and hand hockey.
February 2025 - Trip to Upper Shirley High
The children in Year 6 visited Upper Shirley High to watch their production of High School Musical. They enjoyed seeing past pupils from Wordsworth Primary School performing on the stage. Some children are looking forward to studying Performing Arts when they begin their secondary school journey in September.
Bringing Learning to Life
Year R had some sneaky visitors in their classrooms, and they were caught on CCTV. This inspired them to make their own Gingerbread People.
Year 6 study the Romans in History. They made their own Legionary shields. They enjoyed practising making different formations with shields, just like the Roman army!

Welcome to the Nursery
Early Years
Welcome to Our Nursery
At Wordsworth Nursery we take children from 2-4 years old, when they will move on to school and can apply to join our Reception classes. We are a diverse and inclusive setting, maintaining positive links with our local community.
We have a passionate and dedicated team of staff with a wealth of experience in Early Years who provide an exciting and varied curriculum, supporting children in all 7 areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) to develop at their own pace. We believe that all children should have the chance to learn and play in a safe and stimulating environment, with access to quality indoor and outdoor provision. We provide a mixture of planned activities and free flow, in the moment, child-led play, embedding the Wordsworth Primary School values of; learning, trust, community, nurture and empowerment.
Our Nursery children have access to all areas of the Wordsworth Primary School site including our school field and nature zone, providing them with more opportunities to explore the natural world and enhance their physical development.
We work closely with the Reception team to ensure a smooth and positive transition into school.

We maintain a waiting list of applications, in date of birth order and we work through the list throughout the year, depending on the spaces available.
For more information and to check your eligibility for funding options please visit: Childcare Choices.

Attendance
Information for Parents
School Attendance Matters
Every moment in school counts and days missed add up quickly. Evidence shows that pupils who have good attendance enjoy better wellbeing and school performance than those who don't.
At Wordsworth Primary school we have been working hard to improve our attendance and are pleased to say that our overall attendance to date for this academic year (2024) is 94.6% which is within national guidelines.
All children are expected to attend school EVERYDAY throughout the academic year in order to maximise their learning opportunities. We hope that everyone will join us in attempting to improve this year by following the guidelines below:
School Opening Times
School gates open at 8.40am until 8.50am; please ensure your child arrives in between those times. Children should be in classes ready to start their learning at 8.55am.
After 8.50am, children must enter the school via the main school office to be signed in. If your child arrives after 9.15am, they will be marked as unauthorised absence for the morning session.
School Gates Open at:
Celebrating Attendance
We reward good attendance with class certificates on a weekly basis, and it is celebrated in an assembly. Each week, the class with the highest attendance receives our attendance certificate and every child is recognised for their winning class attendance.
Attendance Superstars
On a weekly basis, one child from every year group is recognised for their commitment to learning and celebrating their success with improved attendance and punctuality.
Notification of Absence
Attendance Matters
It can be tricky to decide whether to keep your child absent from school when they are unwell. As a parent, when thinking should I keep my child off school due to mild illness? please use the NHS link below to support with making the right decision.
Is My Child Too Ill For School
We know that illness is unavoidable and to be expected. However, it is very important to inform the school on the first day of absence with the reason, either by telephone (023 8077 6397) by 9:30am or in person at the school office. Medicine can be given to children at school as long as a medicine form is completed, and all medicines must be in their original boxes.
We expect ALL appointments, with the exception of hospital appointments, to be made outside of normal school hours.
Children can sometimes feel a little bit worried about going to school. Mostly, this is a very normal emotion.
It’s important to recognise that going into school can help children to feel less worried than letting them stay at home.
If your child is anxious over several weeks, talk to us about how we can support you.
We have put together some useful links on the Education Hub on mental health support which you may find helpful.
If you wish to take your child out of school for any period of time, a leave of absence form (available from the office only) should be completed and returned to Mrs Smith, our Attendance Lead.
Please be aware that holiday requests can no longer be authorised. We will only be able to authorise leave of absence in exceptional circumstances.
There may be occasions when a child needs to leave the premises in school time for appointments. It is helpful if the school can be advised in advance and parents are asked to come to the main office to sign their child out. Children are never released from school unaccompanied.
By law, the Governors are required to report on the number of unauthorised absences each year. It is therefore very important to keep the school informed of the reasons for all absences. Attendance is monitored by the Headteacher and the Jeffery's Education Partnership (JEP), which includes regular visits from the JEP Attendance Support Officer who monitors attendance and punctuality. Very low attendance can lead to fixed penalty notices.
Managing Attendance
All of the schools within the Jeffery's Education Partnership have agreed template letters and protocols for managing attendance.
On a half-term basis or as required letters are sent out to parents of those pupils falling below certain levels. This approach is applied across the whole school regardless of the child's age. A child does not become compulsory school aged until they turn 5, however, once a child has been admitted to school they are filling a school place and are expected to attend every day possible. Ofsted place a high level of importance on school attendance and hence so do we as a school. The below protocol allows the school to ensure that they can evidence to Ofsted that we manage attendance effectively.
The schools within Jeffery's Education Partnership have two agreed threshold or distributions of letters to parents and guardians:
When the school has concerns of a serious nature a meeting with the Inclusion Lead and the Attendance Lead to discuss and to establish how we can support the family to improve attendance. If necessary the school will refer attendance concerns to the Jeffery's Education Partnership Attendance Support Officer.
For information and guidance about Attendance, please click here to access Southampton City Council's website.
A copy of our attendance policy can be found below.

School Meals & Lunches
Information for Parents
School Meals & Lunches
Dolce are Wordsworth Primary School's chosen meal provider. Dolce are determined to offer the children of Wordsworth Primary School an excellent service, ensuring that every child enjoys their meal and has the energy to learn in the afternoons.
Dolce offer new menus each term which are cooked from raw ingredients and allow parents/carers and pupils to pre-order their meals from home, on the move or in the classroom.
The cost of a school dinner will is £2.80 per day (£14.00 per week).
If you have any questions, comments or suggestions regarding school meals, allergens, payments etc, please do not hesitate to contact Dolce Customer Care Monday to Friday 8am to 5pm, on 01942 707709 or by email to customercare@dolce.co.uk Dolce are always happy to hear from you.
SchoolGrid Account
If you would like your child to have school meals, you will need a SchoolGrid account. You will receive an email from SchoolGrid, our software providers, with all of your necessary login details. By accessing SchoolGrid online you will be able to pre order meals, view recipes, allergens, ingredients and make payments.
SchoolGrid is the Software provider Dolce use. If you experience any technical issues with access to SchoolGrid, please contact SchoolGrid technical support on 01506 300310 or by email to support@schoolgrid.co.uk.
